s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiac arrest with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and hemodynamic collapse
salient_findings: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
key_facts: 34-year-old White woman with a history of obesity
Presented after an unwitnessed cardiac arrest
Required mechanical intubation for airway protection
Developed atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
Experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions
Troponin T: 0.847 µg/L (elevated)
Troponin I: 0.13 ng/mL (elevated)
Urine toxicology, alcohol, and acetaminophen screening results were negative
ECG showed sinus tachycardia with heart rate 101 beats/min, QTc 443 ms
Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal biventricular size and function
Diagnostic coronary angiogram: no obstructive coronary artery disease
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: mild left ventricular and left atrial dilation, preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (62%)
Electroencephalogram showed status epilepticus

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed QTc 443 ms, which is a risk factor for torsades de pointes and ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ventricular fibrillation with no clear underlying cause

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation, which can be associated with this condition

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although not directly implicated, it is a common cause of sudden cardiac death and ventricular tachycardia in young adults

raw.rationale: The patient experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is a hallmark of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. The normal cardiac structure and function, as well as the absence of other clear causes of ventricular arrhythmias, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc interval was mildly prolonged but not significantly long enough to be diagnostic of Long QT syndrome, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this condition.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: While the patient did experience ventricular fibrillation, the presence of triggering premature ventricular contractions suggests a more specific underlying condition like catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed mild left ventricular and left atrial dilation but no significant right ventricular involvement or fibrofatty replacement, which is characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging did not show significant left ventricular hypertrophy, which is a key feature of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
